mainTopic: The date of מתן תורה (the dispute between the רבנן and רבי יוסי), followed by אגדות about Israel's acceptance of the תורה and the praise of נעשה ונשמע.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a calendar answer about the date of מתן תורה: did it happen on 6 סיון, as the רבנן say, or on 7 סיון, as רבי יוסי says? A ברייתא from סדר עולם puts ראש חודש סיון on Monday, but רבי יוסי answers that it follows the רבנן. A ברייתא in רבי יוסי's own name says משה 'had no time' on the sixth. The גמרא explains this as שבת preparation, not מתן תורה. A Galilean's דרשה about 'threes' is shown to follow the רבנן. Then the גמרא turns to אגדות about מתן תורה: the mountain held over Israel like a tub, the claim of force this raises, and its fix through the willing acceptance in the days of אחשורוש. Next comes ריש לקיש's teaching that all of creation depended on Israel accepting the תורה. A series of teachings then praises Israel for saying נעשה before נשמע: the two crowns, the angels' secret, and the apple tree. The amud ends with a מין mocking רבא as one of a rash nation, and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How the רבנן's calendar works out
steps.stepSummary: The tail of an earlier answer: according to the רבנן, that year had eight short (29-day) months.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, they made eight months lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer it began on the previous amud. It explains how each view's calendar works for that year: רבי יוסי counts seven short months, and the רבנן count eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish month has either 29 days (חסר, short) or 30 days (מלא, full). By adjusting how many months were short, both views can fit the known days of the week. That is how the earlier calendar challenge was answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the majority view, opposing רבי יוסי)

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, they established eight lacking months.
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from just before: according to רבי יוסי they made seven lacking months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer earlier.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Calendar adjustment: the count of short months differs for each view
steps.terutzMaskana: Both views can fit the calendar facts by assuming a different number of short months.

steps.title: סדר עולם puts ראש חודש סיון on Monday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in סדר עולם says יציאת מצרים (15 ניסן) was on Friday. Counting forward places ראש חודש סיון on Monday, which contradicts רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: it was taught in סדר עולם that in the ניסן when Israel left Egypt, they slaughtered their פסח offerings on the 14th and left on the 15th, and that day was a Friday. Since ראש חודש ניסן was on Friday, ראש חודש אייר was on Sunday and סיון on Monday. This is difficult for רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבי יוסי. The source's calendar math puts ראש חודש סיון on Monday, but רבי יוסי says it was Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 1st and the 15th of a month always fall on the same weekday, so ראש חודש ניסן was also a Friday. ניסן has 30 days, so ראש חודש אייר was Sunday. אייר has 29 days, so ראש חודש סיון was Monday. This matches the רבנן, not רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source used as proof or challenge)
An early work of historical chronology, built on a ברייתא
The beginning of the month (ראש חודש)

steps.confusionAlert: The text says ראש חודש ניסן was on Friday because the 1st and the 15th are always the same weekday. It is not saying the Exodus happened on the 1st.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in Seder Olam:
The Nissan in which Israel left Egypt:
on the fourteenth they slaughtered their Pesach offerings,
on the fifteenth they left,
and that day was Friday.
And since Rosh Chodesh Nissan was on Friday,
phrases.notes: The 1st and the 15th share the same weekday.

phrases.english: Rosh Chodesh Iyar was on Sunday,
and Sivan was on Monday,
this is difficult for Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יוסי from a chronology source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that ראש חודש סיון was on Sunday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting from the Friday Exodus with standard month lengths places ראש חודש סיון on Monday.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: that source follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that this ברייתא simply follows the view of the רבנן, so it does not bind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי can tell you: Whose view is this? It is the רבנן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא matches the רבנן's calendar, and רבי יוסי never agreed to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is not a neutral fact that everyone accepts. It reflects one side of the dispute. So it cannot be used to disprove the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (introduces a defense)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei can say to you:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: הָא מַנִּי — רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to the opposing view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא states an agreed-upon fact that all must accept.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, so it poses no difficulty to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's account of משה's trips up the mountain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי describing when משה went up and down הר סיני in the first days of סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי says: On the second day משה went up and came down; on the third he went up and came down; on the fourth he came down and did not go up again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source, this time in רבי יוסי's own name. This sets up a new challenge that comes a few lines later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists משה's movements day by day in early סיון. The question will be what happened on the sixth day, and what that tells us about the date of מתן תורה.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yosei says:
On the second, Moshe went up and came down,
on the third, he went up and came down,
on the fourth, he came down and did not go up again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new source to test רבי יוסי again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה went up and down on the 2nd and 3rd of סיון, and on the 4th came down without going up again.

steps.title: How could he come down without going up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the wording 'on the fourth he came down' makes no sense if he never went up that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since he did not go up, from where did he come down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's wording. You cannot come down a mountain you did not climb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a challenge to the text itself, not to anyone's opinion. It shows the ברייתא's wording needs to be fixed.

phrases.english: And since he did not go up, from where did he come down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'on the fourth he came down and did not go up again'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Coming down requires having gone up first.

steps.title: Corrected text: the fourth, fifth, and sixth days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected: on the fourth he went up and came down, on the fifth he built a מזבח and brought a קרבן, and on the sixth he had no time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: on the fourth he went up and came down; on the fifth he built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it; on the sixth he had no free time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it makes sense. The corrected text adds what happened on the fifth and sixth days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth day now matches the earlier days: he went up and came down. The key new detail is that on the sixth day משה 'had no time', which the גמרא will now look into.

phrases.english: Rather: on the fourth he went up and came down,
on the fifth he built an altar
and offered a sacrifice on it,
on the sixth he had no free time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem in step 5 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On the fourth he only came down.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the fourth he went up and came down; the 5th and 6th days are then described.

steps.title: Was he busy on the sixth because the תורה was given?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests משה had no time on the sixth because the תורה was given that day. That would match the רבנן and contradict רבי יוסי, in his own ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not because of the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי from his own words. Being busy on the sixth suggests that מתן תורה was on 6 סיון, but רבי יוסי says the 7th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strongest reason משה would have 'no time' is that the תורה itself was being given. If so, the date was the 6th, as the רבנן hold. That would make רבי יוסי contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (a suggested reading used as a challenge)

phrases.english: Is it not because of the Torah?
phrases.notes: The suggestion is that the תורה was given on the sixth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a challenging inference from the corrected ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that the תורה was given on 7 סיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'No time on the sixth' implies מתן תורה was on the sixth, as the רבנן say.

steps.title: No: he was busy preparing for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. According to רבי יוסי the sixth was Friday, so משה was busy preparing for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, because of the effort of preparing for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. There is another reason משה had no time on the sixth: it was Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, ראש חודש סיון was Sunday, so the 6th was Friday and the 7th, the day of מתן תורה, was שבת. Being busy on Friday is easily explained by שבת preparation. So the ברייתא fits רבי יוסי after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The effort of preparing for שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not refute רבי יוסי. For him, 6 סיון was Friday, busy with שבת preparation, and the תורה was given on the 7th, on שבת.

phrases.english: No, because of the effort of preparing for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reason given for being busy, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being busy on the sixth can be explained by שבת preparation, not necessarily by מתן תורה.

steps.title: The Galilean's דרשה about 'threes'
steps.stepSummary: A Galilean taught before רב חסדא: Blessed is ה׳, who gave a threefold תורה to a threefold nation, through a third child, on the third day, in the third month.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Galilean expounded before רב חסדא: Blessed is the Merciful One who gave a threefold תורה, to a threefold people, through a third-born, on the third day, in the third month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a beautiful דרשה praising ה׳ for the many 'threes' in מתן תורה. It sets up the question of which view it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The threes are: תורה, נביאים, and כתובים; כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים; משה, born third after מרים and אהרן; the third day of separation before מתן תורה; and סיון, the third month. The phrase 'third day' is the detail that matters for the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A Galilean (a man from the Galil)

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַשׁ הַהוּא גָּלִילָאָה עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: A certain Galilean expounded before Rav Chisda:
Blessed is the Merciful One who gave a threefold Torah,
to a threefold people,
through a third-born,
phrases.notes: משה, born after מרים and אהרן.

phrases.english: on the third day,
in the third month.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ הַהוּא גָּלִילָאָה עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, aggadic source related to the date of מתן תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה was given amid a pattern of threes, including 'on the third day'.

steps.title: The דרשה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the דרשה as following the רבנן, who hold the תורה came on the third day of separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which view the דרשה follows and answers: the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold there were three days of separation, so the תורה came on the third day, which was 6 סיון. רבי יוסי holds משה added a day, making it the fourth day, so the דרשה's 'third day' does not fit him.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'third day' in the Galilean's דרשה follows the רבנן: three days of separation, with the תורה given on 6 סיון.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which side of the dispute the drasha in step 9 follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Galilean's דרשה follows the רבנן's view of מתן תורה on the third day of separation.

steps.title: The mountain held over Israel like a tub
steps.stepSummary: רב אבדימי בר חמא בר חסא reads 'בתחתית ההר' literally: the people stood underneath the mountain, which הקב״ה held over them, and they were told to accept the תורה or be buried there.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they stood at the bottom of the mountain.' רב אבדימי בר חמא בר חסא said: This teaches that הקב״ה turned the mountain over them like a tub and said: If you accept the תורה, good. If not, there will be your burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about מתן תורה. רב אבדימי reads the פסוק as saying the people stood literally under the mountain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'בתחתית ההר' is 'at the foot of the mountain.' רב אבדימי reads it as 'underneath the mountain.' This creates a picture of the תורה being accepted under pressure, and the next two steps react to that picture.

keyTerms.meaning: At the bottom of the mountain. Here it is read as 'underneath the mountain.'
Turned over, held upside down above

phrases.english: 'And they stood at the bottom of the mountain,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַבְדִּימִי בַּר חָמָא בַּר חַסָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Avdimi bar Chama bar Chasa said:
This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, turned over
the mountain above them like a tub,
and He said to them:
If you accept the Torah, good,
and if not, there will be your burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ בְּתַחְתִּית הָהָר אָמַר רַב אַבְדִּימִי בַּר חָמָא בַּר חַסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dating of מתן תורה to a new אגדה about how the תורה was accepted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel accepted the תורה with the mountain held over them as a threat.

steps.title: This gives a claim against the תורה's obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב notes that if the תורה was accepted by force, Israel has a strong legal claim that the acceptance is not binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: From here there is a big protest-claim against the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב raises a problem that comes out of רב אבדימי's teaching. If the people were forced, maybe they are not bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודעא is a formal declaration that an agreement was made under pressure, and such a declaration cancels the agreement. If the תורה was accepted under the mountain, Israel could say the agreement was forced and can be cancelled. This sets up רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A formal declaration that an agreement was made under pressure, which makes it cancellable

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying the תורה is not binding. He is pointing out a legal weakness that the forced acceptance would create, and רבא closes that gap in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
From here there is a great protest-claim against the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling legal consequence from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the acceptance of the תורה at סיני is binding
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An agreement made under pressure can be cancelled. The mountain held overhead is pressure, so the obligation looks weak.

steps.title: The תורה was accepted again willingly in the time of אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even so, the Jews accepted the תורה again by choice in the days of אחשורוש, as the מגילה says 'קימו וקבלו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even so, they accepted it again in the days of אחשורוש, as it says 'the Jews upheld and accepted.' They upheld what they had already accepted before.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב אחא's problem. A later, voluntary acceptance fixes the forced one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in אסתר lists 'קימו' (upheld) before 'קבלו' (accepted). רבא reads it as: they now upheld willingly what they had accepted earlier at סיני. That willing acceptance removes the claim of force.

keyTerms.meaning: The Persian king in the story of פורים

steps.whatToRemember: The forced acceptance at סיני, which was open to a מודעא, was later confirmed by a free acceptance in the time of פורים.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲדוּר קַבְּלוּהָ
phrases.english: Even so, they accepted it again
in the days of Achashverosh,
as it is written: 'The Jews upheld and accepted' —
they upheld what they had already accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הֲדוּר קַבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the claim raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A later event fixes the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forced acceptance at סיני leaves the תורה open to a claim of force.
steps.terutzMaskana: The willing acceptance in the days of אחשורוש makes the obligation fully binding.

steps.title: How can the earth be both afraid and quiet?
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה points to a פסוק in תהלים that says the earth feared and was quiet, and asks how both can be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: What is the meaning of 'From heaven You made judgment heard; the earth feared and was quiet'? If it feared, why was it quiet? And if it was quiet, why did it fear?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. חזקיה asks how a פסוק can describe the earth with two opposite reactions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fear suggests trembling, and quiet suggests calm, so the two words seem to contradict each other. The 'judgment from heaven' refers to מתן תורה. The next step solves the contradiction.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'From heaven You made judgment heard;
the earth feared and was quiet'?
If it feared, why was it quiet?
And if it was quiet, why did it fear?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה about the effect of מתן תורה on the world.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the earth can be described as both afraid and calm

steps.title: First it feared, and in the end it was calm
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that the two words describe two different times: first fear, then calm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, at first it feared, and in the end it was quiet.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה solves the contradiction by putting the two reactions in order, one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction once we see that the earth feared before the תורה was accepted and calmed down afterward. This answer leads to the next question: what was the earth afraid of?

phrases.english: Rather, at first it feared
and in the end it was quiet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fear came first and the calm came afterward.

steps.title: Why was the earth afraid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what caused the earth's fear before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did it fear?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. It prepares the next step, which explains the cause of the fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the order of the reactions is not enough. We still need a reason the earth would be afraid at all, and the answer comes from ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: And why did it fear?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the earth's fear

steps.title: Creation depended on Israel accepting the Torah
steps.stepSummary: Following ריש לקיש, the extra ה in 'יום השישי' teaches that הקב״ה made all of creation conditional on Israel accepting the תורה. So the earth feared it might go back to chaos.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of 'And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day'? Why do I need the extra ה? It teaches that הקב״ה made a condition with the works of creation and said to them: If Israel accepts the תורה, you will continue to exist. If not, I will return you to emptiness and chaos.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the earth was afraid by quoting ריש לקיש. The whole world's existence was on the line until Israel accepted the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other days of creation are written without 'ה', but the sixth day says 'השישי'. ריש לקיש reads that ה as pointing to 'the sixth' day of סיון, the day the תורה was given. So the earth trembled until the תורה was accepted, and once it was accepted the earth calmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Emptiness and chaos, the state before creation

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the תורה as the purpose of the whole world. Creation itself only lasts because Israel accepted it.

phrases.english: As Reish Lakish taught.
For Reish Lakish said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day'?
Why do I need the extra letter heh?
It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a condition
with the works of creation and said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִים הַתּוֹרָה — אַתֶּם מִתְקַיְּימִין,
phrases.english: If Israel accepts the Torah, you will continue to exist,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֲנִי מַחֲזִיר אֶתְכֶם לְתוֹהוּ וָבוֹהוּ.
phrases.english: and if not, I will return you to emptiness and chaos.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Creation was conditional on Israel accepting the תורה, so the earth feared until they accepted it.

steps.title: Two crowns for נעשה ונשמע, removed after the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי teaches that angels gave each Jew two crowns for saying נעשה before נשמע. After the חטא העגל, angels of destruction took the crowns away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימאי taught: When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear', 600,000 ministering angels came and tied two crowns onto each person in Israel, one for 'we will do' and one for 'we will hear'. When Israel sinned, 1,200,000 angels of destruction came down and removed them, as it says: 'The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from הר חורב.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins about the greatness of saying נעשה before נשמע. רבי סימאי describes the reward of crowns and how it was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'we will do' before even hearing the details showed complete trust, and each statement earned its own crown. After the חטא העגל, twice as many destroying angels came, one for each crown, and took them back. The proof is the פסוק about Israel removing their 'ornaments'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will do and we will hear', Israel's answer at סיני

phrases.english: Rabbi Simai taught:
When Israel put first
'we will do' before 'we will hear,'

phrases.aramaic: בָּאוּ שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת,
phrases.english: 600,000 ministering angels came,
and to each and every one of Israel
they tied two crowns,
one for 'we will do'
and one for 'we will hear.'
And once Israel sinned,

phrases.aramaic: יָרְדוּ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים רִיבּוֹא מַלְאֲכֵי חַבָּלָה וּפֵירְקוּם,
phrases.english: 1,200,000 angels of destruction came down and removed them,
as it says: 'And the children of Israel stripped themselves
of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי סִימַאי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה about the reward for נעשה ונשמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel received two crowns for נעשה ונשמע and lost them after the חטא העגל.

steps.title: At Horeb they received them, at Horeb they lost them
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא reads 'מהר חורב' as saying that the crowns were both put on and taken off at חורב, which is הר סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: At חורב they put them on, and at חורב they took them off. At חורב they put them on, as we said. At חורב they took them off, as it is written: 'And the children of Israel stripped themselves.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא adds a point to רבי סימאי's teaching. The same place saw both the gain and the loss of the crowns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חורב is another name for הר סיני. The crowns were given there at מתן תורה, and the פסוק of 'stripping' also mentions חורב. So both events are tied to the same mountain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
At Horeb they put them on, at Horeb they took them off.
At Horeb they put them on, as we said;
at Horeb they took them off, as it is written:
'And the children of Israel stripped themselves, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crowns were both given and removed at חורב.

steps.title: משה merited and took all the crowns
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says משה earned all the crowns that were taken away. He learns this from the next פסוק, 'ומשה יקח את האהל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: משה merited all of them and took them. For right next to it is written: 'And משה would take the tent.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us where the removed crowns went: to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק right after the removal of the ornaments says 'ומשה יקח'. Because the two פסוקים are next to each other, רבי יוחנן reads it as משה taking what Israel lost. The word אהל hints at a shining glow.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is placed right next to it
Tent. Here it hints at a glow of light.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And Moshe merited all of them and took them.
For right next to it is written:
'And Moshe would take the tent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the crowns from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה received all the crowns that Israel lost.

steps.title: The crowns will be returned in the future
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says הקב״ה will give the crowns back to Israel in the future, reading 'שמחת עולם על ראשם' as 'the joy from long ago on their heads'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: In the future הקב״ה will return them to us, as it says: 'And the redeemed of ה׳ will return and come to ציון with song, and everlasting joy on their heads.' The joy they had long ago will be on their heads.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש ends the crowns story on a hopeful note: Israel will get them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'שמחת עולם' as 'joy from מעולם', meaning joy from long ago. Because it sits 'on their heads', it refers to the crowns from סיני coming back.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לָנוּ,
phrases.english: In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will return them to us,
as it says: 'And the redeemed of ה׳ will return
and come to Zion with song,
and everlasting joy upon their heads' —
the joy from long ago will be upon their heads.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the crowns story: given, removed, taken by משה, and returned in the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future הקב״ה will return the crowns to Israel.

steps.title: נעשה before נשמע is the secret of the angels
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says a בת קול praised Israel for discovering the angels' secret of doing before hearing, as seen in a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear', a heavenly voice came out and said: Who revealed to My children this secret that the ministering angels use? As it is written: 'Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, to listen to the voice of His word.' First it says 'do', and then 'listen'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings another praise of נעשה ונשמע. Israel acted like the angels, who carry out ה׳'s word before hearing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'עושי דברו' (doing His word) comes before 'לשמוע' (listening). So the angels' way is to commit to doing first. Israel did the same thing at סיני, which amazed even heaven.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear,'
a heavenly voice came out and said to them:
Who revealed to My children this secret
that the ministering angels use?
As it is written: 'Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength,
who do His word, to listen to the voice of His word' —
first 'do,' and afterward 'listen.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another praise of נעשה ונשמע, this time comparing Israel to the angels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting doing before hearing is the angels' way, and Israel adopted it at סיני.

steps.title: Israel is like the apple tree: fruit before leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that Israel is compared to an apple tree because its fruit appears before its leaves, just as Israel put נעשה before נשמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: What is the meaning of 'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest'? Why is Israel compared to an apple tree? To teach you: just as this apple tree has its fruit before its leaves, so too Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear'.
steps.whatsHappening: This passage ends with a final praise of נעשה ונשמע, this time comparing Israel to an apple tree from שיר השירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The apple tree was believed to produce its fruit before its leaves, the opposite of the normal order. The fruit stands for doing, and the leaves stand for the preparation of hearing. So Israel, like the apple tree, did the main thing first.

keyTerms.meaning: Trees of the forest (שיר השירים ב:ג)
Its fruit comes before its leaves

steps.whatToRemember: This section praises Israel for saying נעשה before נשמע. They earned crowns, which were lost after the sin, taken by משה, and will return in the future. They followed the way of the angels, and they are like the apple tree whose fruit comes before its leaves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the meaning of what is written: 'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, etc.'?
Why is Israel compared to an apple tree?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֶם לְעָלָיו,
phrases.english: just as this apple tree has its fruit before its leaves,
so too Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one more image for נעשה before נשמע, completing the series of praises.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel is like the apple tree, whose fruit comes before its leaves, because they put doing before hearing.

steps.title: A heretic sees רבא bleeding while learning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the scene: a מין sees רבא so absorbed in learning that he squeezes his own fingers until they bleed, without noticing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic saw רבא deep in study of a teaching. רבא's fingers were under his leg, and he was pressing on them so hard that they were spurting blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story. This step sets up the scene for the מין's attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story follows right after the teachings praising Israel for saying נעשה before נשמע. רבא's total focus on learning, so strong he does not feel pain, shows that same full commitment. The מין is about to read this devotion as foolish rashness.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic (someone who rejects Jewish belief)

phrases.english: A certain heretic who saw Rava
that he was immersed in studying a teaching
and his fingers were placed under his leg
and he was squeezing them
and his fingers were spurting blood.
phrases.notes: רבא was so absorbed that he did not notice

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the נעשה ונשמע theme with a story that shows it in action
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא was so devoted to learning that he did not feel his own fingers bleeding.

steps.title: The heretic mocks Israel as a rash nation
steps.stepSummary: The מין mocks Israel for saying נעשה before נשמע. He says they are still rash, and that a sensible people would first listen and only then decide whether to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to רבא: You rash nation, who put your mouths before your ears! You are still acting rashly. You should first have listened. Then, if you could keep it, you would accept it, and if not, you would not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The מין attacks Israel's acceptance of the תורה. He calls נעשה ונשמע reckless, and he points to רבא's bleeding fingers as proof that Jews still act without thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting 'mouths before ears' means Israel said 'we will do', a promise made with the mouth, before 'we will hear', which is done with the ears. The מין turns the praise from the earlier steps into an insult. He argues that the wise approach is to check the terms first and only then commit.

keyTerms.meaning: Your mouths before your ears (doing before hearing)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Mouths before ears' is not about talking too much. It refers to Israel saying נעשה (a promise with the mouth) before נשמע (hearing).

phrases.english: He said to him: Impulsive nation,
who put your mouths before your ears,
you still remain in your impulsiveness.
phrases.notes: He points to רבא's bleeding as proof

phrases.english: First you should have listened;
if you are able, accept;
and if not, do not accept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The מין uses the scene from step 24 to attack the נעשה ונשמע idea
steps.kashyaTarget: Israel's acceptance of the תורה with נעשה before נשמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Committing before you know what you are committing to is reckless. A wise person checks first whether he can keep it.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to reply to the מין with the word 'we'. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We…
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer to the מין. This passage stops here, so this step only opens the reply that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By starting with 'אנן' (we), רבא signals that he will answer on behalf of Israel. Given the earlier steps, we can expect him to defend Israel's trust in הקב״ה, which is not like a careful business deal where one checks the terms first. The full answer appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him: We…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא starts to respond to the מין's attack
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defense of נעשה ונשמע (only the opening word appears here; the rest of the answer is on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting without hearing first is reckless.
steps.terutzMaskana: To be completed on the next amud.
